result.instructions: FieldCraft turns geometry into finite element models and solves them. The model stores SI and shows and takes numbers in its display units (default mm-t-s-N-MPa with °C: E in MPa, density in t/mm³, forces in N; `model.units` changes them, and a value may carry its unit: "210 GPa"); Z is up. A typical analysis: `open` a .solidcraft design (or a .fieldcraft model, or a face-tagged .3mf); `inspect_model` for its bodies and their persistent face names; `mesh` (method tet: {body, tolerance}); then `execute` the model definition commands (model.set.create {name, geometry: [{body, face}]}, model.material.create, model.section.create, model.boundary_condition.create, model.load.create, model.step.create — list_commands shows each one's parameters); `check_model`; `solve` (static, nonlinear, frequency, buckle, explicit, fluid, heat); `show_results` (field: displacement, von_mises…; its reply has the field's range) and `probe` / `reactions` for numbers; `screenshot` to look; `save` or `write_deck` (abaqus, nastran, lsdyna). Partitions: geometry.datum makes a datum plane, geometry.partition cuts the design's bodies into cells by it (cut faces partition:<name>:a|b; kept in the model and applied again when the design opens); `mesh` method cells meshes the cells each with its own method, method mirror reflects a meshed half across a datum plane into one conforming mesh; model.boundary_condition.symmetry holds a half model on its symmetry plane (file.sample crank-mirror shows the partition, half-mesh and mirror sequence). Edge seeds: mesh.seed.edge {edges: [{body, edge}], count | size, bias?, constraint?} fixes the element count along design edges (inspect_model lists the edge names): seed a thin section's thickness, a fillet or hole edge (biased toward the stress raiser), and partition cells' shared edges so their counts match. Failures leave the model unchanged and name what to fix. Backend: a headless in-process FieldCraft session (no window; screenshots drawn offscreen with the viewport's GPU pipeline, or on the CPU without a GPU).
